To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified a cDNA for a light-induced, chloroplast-specific, glycine-rich protein, which is a novel member of a family of light-induced proteins, and which contains a putative transmembrane domain.
we have cloned a novel light-induced gene from the dicotyledon Chenopodium rubram which encodes a glycine-rich protein with an unusual domain structure.
we have cloned and sequenced a light-induced glycine rich protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes which are specifically induced during chloroplast development.
the molecular mechanisms of light-regulated gene expression.
the molecular analysis of light-induced gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the cDNA sequence for the novel light-induced glycinerich protein (LIGP1) has been determined and that the protein contains a hydrophobic alpha helix and six repeats with a consensus motif of 6 amino acids.
the protein is a light-induced chloroplast protein, which is encoded in the nucleus, synthesized on cytoplasmic ribosomes, and imported into the chloroplasts (4).
the sequence of the clone HC1 is not a typical light-induced gene.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the light-induced gene HC1 encodes for a protein which is probably located in the thylakoid membrane.
a light-induced glycine rich protein with a putative role as membrane binding protein is synthesized during chloroplast development in C.rubrum.
a novel class of light-induced genes has been identified, which are probably not involved in the regulation of photosynthetic processes, but in the differentiation and/or assembly of the plastids.
